name: open-tyrian
why: An open-source port of a classic 1995 shoot-em-up; excellent retro game, though it is not a terminal game.

brief.what_it_is: OpenTyrian is an open-source port of the 1995 DOS vertical-scrolling arcade shooter Tyrian. You play Trent Hawkins, a fighter pilot hired to fight MicroSol in the year 20,031. It offers a story mode, one- and two-player arcade modes, and networked multiplayer. It is a graphical game with no terminal interface: you launch it and play in a window, with optional joystick or gamepad input. Game data comes from the freeware Tyrian 2.1 files, which the release builds bundle.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no explicit motivation. It presents the project as an open-source port of the original DOS game, so it keeps Tyrian playable on modern systems.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It says the game reads the Tyrian 2.1 data files from a search path (a --data directory, a data folder next to the executable, a system directory, or the current directory). For network play, it uses UDP port 1333 and UDP hole punching, so most players do not need to open ports.

commands_seen.context: Builds OpenTyrian from source. Requires a C99 compiler, GNU make, pkg-config, SDL2, and optionally SDL2_net for network play.
Launches the game after extracting a Linux release tarball.

Starts a networked game manually. Both players run it at the same time. HOSTNAME is the opponent's IP address, NUMBER is 1 or 2 to pick a ship, and NAME is your alias. There is no arena or matchmaking.

brief.install_notes: Release builds for Windows (zip, run opentyrian.exe), macOS (universal zip, open OpenTyrian.app) and Linux (tar.gz, run ./opentyrian) include the freeware Tyrian 2.1 data, so nothing else is needed. The macOS app is not notarized: if Gatekeeper blocks it, right-click, choose Open, and confirm once. To build from source you need the Tyrian 2.1 data (tyrian21.zip from camanis.net, lowercase filenames) placed in a searched directory, or pointed to with --data=DIR. Network play is enabled automatically when SDL2_net is found. The README also mentions a Visual Studio solution in visualc/. Configuration lives in %APPDATA%\OpenTyrian on Windows and in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opentyrian or ~/.config/opentyrian on macOS and Linux. Putting an opentyrian.cfg next to the executable on Windows or Linux makes it store config and saves there instead.
brief.standout: It is a faithful port of a classic DOS shooter that still ships the freeware Tyrian 2.1 data in its release builds, so it runs with no separate purchase or download. Its multiplayer uses UDP hole punching so that most players need no port forwarding.
brief.status: unknown. The README has no release dates, changelog, or commit history, and I did not check the releases page, so I cannot confirm whether the project is active. It does list live IRC and forum links.
brief.caveats: The brew caveat says save games go to ~/.opentyrian, but the README puts saves and config in ~/.config/opentyrian (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opentyrian) on macOS and Linux. Treat the README as the authority unless the brew formula says otherwise. The macOS app is not notarized, so Gatekeeper may block it on first run. Networked games must be set up by hand on the command line by both players at once, with no arena. Building from source requires you to supply the Tyrian 2.1 data yourself. The README does not list a license.
quotes: OpenTyrian is an open-source port of the DOS game Tyrian.
Currently OpenTyrian does not have an arena; as such, networked games must be initiated manually via the command line simultaneously by both players.
OpenTyrian uses UDP port 1333 for multiplayer, but in most cases players will not need to open any ports because OpenTyrian makes use of UDP hole punching.
